changes.walking: Progressive walking occupies stick magnitudes up to 0.74, reaching 1.55 m/s before a smooth rise to the approved full-stick pace. The entire slow lower-body gait has overlapping support. A 1.12 s cycle places a real shoe contact during the advancing swing at frame 16, preventing backward approach corrections between slow touches. Full-stick and RB top speeds are preserved.
changes.reserve: Human sprint spending reads the actual RB button every simulation tick, including during selected clips; assistance-requested speed is not a sprint button. Only walking-range non-RB manual locomotion commands are capped by actual manual speed; the native catch-up assist after sprint remains available above that range without spending reserve. CPU reserve follows its own sprint decisions.
changes.cpu: All 21 CPU athletes share the human protective-motion bank and run the bounded neural muscular tracker when moving or under pressure, instead of passive tracking throughout distant runs. Predicted free-ball arrivals orient the receiver toward the ball. Rear impacts are not head cushions.
changes.contacts: Real body contact supplies one physical impulse rather than also receiving a legacy proximity impulse. Positional shell separation is capped, and near teammates have reduced real contact forces.
changes.learned_muscles: A genuinely trained 18-weight, six-unit tanh angular servo controls Bullet upper-body tracking and falling muscles with anatomical and torque limits. It was trained by cross-entropy search on domain-randomized reduced angular dynamics using disjoint native reference files, not full-body RL locomotion or Euphoria.
changes.balance: Accumulated load can select a protective response; the response has a smoother onset and larger bounded envelope. Rendered upper-body compliance is stronger, while leg support and final anatomical projection remain.

learned_motor.algorithm: cross-entropy neural policy search on perturbed angular dynamics
learned_motor.scope: Learned upper-body angular servo with native motion references and domain-randomized reduced dynamics. Not Euphoria, AMP, a trained whole-body locomotion/balance policy, or proof of full-body sim-to-game transfer.

investigated_findings: The first preflight exposed real low-stick root backtracking: a retimed late foot event and an overlong stride let the player overrun a stopped ball. Merely moving the event earlier was insufficient; a normal walking cadence and contact during forward shoe swing eliminated backward steps in the final three-strength rendered test.

A previous rendered brief-pass assertion assumed advance(40) held input for 40 ms. Telemetry is sampled every 100 ms and the game actually measured 120 ms, producing the correct 7.34274 m/s pass. The test now records measured charge, bounds the brief charge and verifies progressive power. No pass-power gameplay code was altered for this assertion.

The earlier first-person procedural comparison measured whole-action peak torso angles differing by 0.01916 rad, just below its 0.02 rad margin. The same raw traces showed mean torso response around actual impact of 0.19574 rad for standing and 0.36612 rad for running; arm means were 0.28580 and 0.43982 rad. The revised test aligns the +/-120 ms contact windows, keeps the original 0.02 rad margins and separately retains rendered anatomical/contact checks. Both cameras were rerun on the final binary.

The broad non-RB speed cap also suppressed the native catch-up assist after sprint, exposing a 3.221 m ball gap in first person. The cap is now confined to the walking range. Actual RB alone still controls reserve spending. The native sprint/release connection is rerun in both cameras, along with the complete regression on the final hash.

The final fixture reruns below preserve the same binary. Their earlier failures and exact reasons for improving fixture/state/telemetry assertions are retained in superseded_test_outcomes; no failed final gameplay check is silently counted as passing.
Only the 32 selected cases above use the exact final native hash; all earlier exploratory builds and failed preflights are excluded from release checks.
limits: Rendered regressions use Linux/X11, a virtual Xbox controller and the OpenAL null driver. Windows is cross-compiled and statically package-validated; actual Windows rendering, physical controller feel and audible balance still require the user PC.

The learned angular servo is trained on a reduced model, not whole-body Bullet rollouts. Held-out results show lower weighted cost and jerk than baselines; the corrected relative-velocity PD has lower tracking RMS than the learned servo. Full-body sim-to-game equivalence is not established.
This is a native animation-driven/Bullet prototype with bounded procedural responses, not proprietary Euphoria/GTA code, a new mocap library or a completed learned locomotion policy.
The approved controlled ground-dribble collision exemption remains. Real skin gates and anatomy checks do not establish universal absence of interpenetration or every possible reception.
Procedural catalogue counts are compatible profiles, not exhaustive visual validation. Physical parameters and biomechanical responses are calibrated game approximations.
